name: Fasnachtshaus Nassereith
kurzbeschreibung: The Fasnachtshaus in Nassereith: award-winning heritage museum dedicated to the Schellerlaufen carnival with over 400 artistic wooden masks crafted by master woodcarvers.
beschreibung:
Overview

The award-winning Fasnachtshaus Nassereith is located on the picturesque Postplatz in the heart of the Tyrolean Oberland municipality of Nassereith (Imst district) at an altitude of around 840 metres. Situated right at the entrance to the Gurgltal valley and along the historic Fernpass route, this modern specialised museum is entirely dedicated to the Nassereither Schellerlaufen. This centuries-old carnival tradition is among the most colourful, expressive, and significant traditional events in the entire Alpine region and has been officially inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in Austria.

Schellerlaufen & Mask Carving Art

According to ancient custom, the Nassereither Schellerlaufen takes place every three years, captivating tens of thousands of spectators. The Fasnachtshaus was opened in 2008 to bring the fascination of this ancient fertility and winter-expulsion ritual to life all year round. The centrepiece of the exhibition is the world's largest and most significant collection of over 400 hand-carved wooden masks (Larven) spanning three centuries. Nassereith is renowned for its unique woodcarving tradition: artists like Franz Josef Falger created masks of unmatched plasticity and masterful emotional expression during the 19th and 20th centuries. On display are the magnificent main figures of the custom in their original silk robes: the proud Sch?ne with a delicate female face, the dignified Scheller with massive bronze bells, the wild Roller, the menacing K?rrner, and the primeval B?ren with their drivers. Large-scale multimedia projections, audio recordings of the rhythmic bell chiming, and historical film footage convey the thrilling energy of the Schellerlaufen.

Visit & Getting There

The Fasnachtshaus Nassereith is open from May to the end of October on Fridays and Sundays from 15:00 to 18:00 (extended opening hours in winter during the carnival season; open year-round for groups of 8 or more by advance reservation). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. ?6.00, seniors approx. ?5.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. ?3.00, young children free; family ticket approx. ?14.00. Holders of the regional Urlaubspass Imst receive discounted admission. Getting there by car: via the Fernpass road B179 or B189 directly to Nassereith; free parking is available at Postplatz or near the community centre. By public transport: take the ?BB train to Imst-Pitztal station, from where VVT bus line 4206 runs every half hour directly to the Nassereith Postplatz stop (just a one-minute walk to the museum).

Tips

The Fasnachtshaus is exemplarily barrier-free and fully wheelchair-accessible; all floors can be reached conveniently via a modern passenger elevator. Be sure to take time for the film screening in the in-house cinema hall to experience the archaic power of the Schellerlaufen up close. After your visit, take a stroll to the idyllic Nassereither See lake at the foot of the rock face, only about a five-minute walk away.
